theme_central: Allah's absolute sovereignty over everything (al-Mulk): life and death created to test who acts best — hence its reputation as protection against the punishment of the grave.
sources_note: 3-4 part structure sourced (historyofislam.com, grokipedia): sovereignty/creation (1-4), fragility of life (5-21), final argumentation (22-30).

branches.title: Allah's sovereignty, perfect creation
branches.resume: Life and death created to test who acts best; seven heavens stacked without the slightest flaw.

children.t: Life and death created to test, seven flawless heavens

branches.title: Stars, Hell, dialogue of the damned
branches.resume: Stars as missiles against the demons; dialogue of Hell's keepers with the damned full of regret.

children.t: Dialogue of Hell's keepers with the damned, regret at not having listened

branches.title: Fearing Allah in secret
branches.resume: Reward promised to whoever fears Allah in secret; He knows the secrets of hearts.

children.t: Fearing Allah in secret rewarded, Allah knows the secrets of hearts

branches.title: Earth subdued, security before the sky
branches.resume: The earth subdued for man to walk and eat from; security before a sky that could collapse.

children.t: Earth subdued for man, security before the sky, fate of the ancient peoples

branches.title: The birds, who can help
branches.resume: Birds that spread and fold their wings; who but Allah could come to the rescue?

children.t: Birds in flight, no help possible but from Allah

branches.title: Walking stooped or upright
branches.resume: Comparison between one who walks with face bowed and one who walks upright on the path.

children.t: Comparison of stooped/upright walking; hearing, sight and hearts created by Allah

branches.title: Closing
branches.resume: Mocking question about the timing; who would bring you clear water if yours were to vanish?

children.t: Timing of the promise, clear water as a final reminder of dependence on Allah
